entities.who_term: Conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma; squamous cell carcinoma of the lacrimal drainage system
entities.why: Neither Milman 2023 nor Pfister 2022 reports this carcinoma in children; Pfister 2022 Table 3 lists no carcinoma among the paediatric eye tumours. It is a picker entry (ruling 1). Milman lists it at the conjunctiva (Table 3) and the lacrimal drainage system (Table 12).

cite.quote: Conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma
Malignant epithelial tumors of the lacrimal drainage system
Eye tumors Conjunctival Neoplasms Hamartomas

entities.who_term: Squamous cell carcinoma with mucinous differentiation (conjunctiva)
entities.why: WHO Eye5 names a squamous cell carcinoma with scattered mucin-containing cells, and no true glands, a squamous cell carcinoma with mucinous differentiation rather than an adenosquamous carcinoma. ICD-O-3.2 prints no term for it. 8070/3 follows the WHO name; Rule K would give the higher code 8480/3 Mucinous adenocarcinoma. The registrar decides.

cite.quote: squamous cell carcinoma with mucinous differentiation
invasive nonkeratinizing squamous cell carcinoma with focal intracytoplasmic mucin
applied only to neoplasms with bi-phenotypic differentiation comprising squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma

entities.who_term: Adenosquamous carcinoma (conjunctiva)
entities.why: Neither Milman 2023 nor Pfister 2022 reports this carcinoma in children; Pfister 2022 Table 3 lists no carcinoma among the paediatric eye tumours. It is a picker entry (ruling 1). WHO Eye5 keeps the term for tumours with both squamous cell carcinoma and true mucin-forming adenocarcinoma.

cite.quote: Conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma Adenosquamous carcinoma
applied only to neoplasms with bi-phenotypic differentiation comprising squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma
invasive adenocarcinoma component is composed of epithelial cells with focal intracytoplasmic mucin

entities.who_term: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma (lacrimal gland, lacrimal drainage system; the Eye4 term for some conjunctival carcinomas)
entities.why: Neither Milman 2023 nor Pfister 2022 reports this carcinoma in children; Pfister 2022 Table 3 lists no carcinoma among the paediatric eye tumours. It is a picker entry (ruling 1). WHO Eye5 lists it in the lacrimal gland and drainage system. At the conjunctiva, Eye4 used adenosquamous carcinoma as the preferred term; a conjunctival report that still says mucoepidermoid carcinoma is coded as written, 8430/3.

cite.quote: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma (MEC)
Malignant lacrimal gland neoplasm characterized by squamous (epidermoid) cells, mucous cells
The term adenosquamous carcinoma, introduced in the Eye4 as the preferred term for mucoepidermoid carcinoma

A report that places the tumour in the conjunctiva itself is a registrar question.

cite.quote: Sebaceous carcinoma, covered in Tumors of the Eyelid chapter, has been removed

ICD-O-3.2 prints the salivary gland sites (C07._, C08._) beside the term; the stated lacrimal gland site wins (Rule H).

entities.who_term: Adenocarcinoma of the ciliary body epithelium

entities.who_term: Medulloepithelioma of the ciliary body (including teratoid medulloepithelioma)

nodes.hint: Choose the strongest evidence in the file. An immunohistochemistry or gene report on its own does not stand in for a histology report. A tumour the file calls possible or suspected is not registrable.

rules_a_to_k.how: ey_site options: 'Eyelid, including the eyelid margin' carries the reason that an eyelid tumour is recorded at the skin of the eyelid (C44.1) and hands the case to the skin tree; 'Eye, part not stated' records C69.9.
ey_site option 'Only a region around the eye (periorbital or periocular)': its reason states that a prefix site is not an ICD-O site and the next screen asks the tissue, falling back to C76.0.
ey_site option 'More than one of these parts, and the report cannot say where the tumour began' records C69.8; the reason states the point of origin cannot be determined.
Referral reasons for lymphoma (ey_surface, ey_lacrimal, ey_intraocular, ey_orbit) state that Group II records the lymphoma at the part of the eye or orbit where it arose.
ey_orbit_histology option 'Myeloid sarcoma': the reason states it is recorded in Group I at the orbit, not at bone marrow.

Exclusion option labels and reasons on the surface and lacrimal screens name the in situ, low-grade and benign behaviours (8077/2, 8077/0, 8070/2, 8500/2, 8940/0). The lacrimal option 'Malignant mixed tumour, or malignant pleomorphic adenoma' codes the stated malignant behaviour (8940/3) and refers it to Group XII.
No eye code depends on grade and no screen in this part offers two grades. Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is graded in the report, but every grade records 8430/3.

Reasons on the picker options for carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma (8941/3, printed site C07/C08) and ductal adenocarcinoma (8500/3, printed site C50) state that the stated lacrimal site wins. The sebaceous carcinoma option (printed site C44) sends the case to the eyelid. Retinoblastoma (printed site C69.2) refers to Group V. The deposit option on every screen applies the clause that the site is used only after a metastasis is ruled out.

Every Milman eye term matches an ICD-O-3.2 term or synonym directly (checked in icdo32.sqlite); no word roots need reordering. ICD-O lists the combination 'mixed adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma' at 8560/3 itself.

Hint on ey_carcinoma_other, the screen that offers both codes: 'If the report names two carcinoma types for one tumour and no single term covers both, choose the one with the higher code number.' Adenosquamous carcinoma needs no Rule K because 8560/3 covers both components. Squamous cell carcinoma with mucinous differentiation is a registrar question (8070/3 by the WHO name, 8480/3 by Rule K).

conflicts.issue: Retinoblastoma is Group V at every eye site and is registered there without tissue, because biopsy is avoided. The eye tree refers it on the evidence gate before the 8000/3 answers; without that option, an imaging-only retinoblastoma would record 8000/3 (XIIb). The router's C69 candidate groups (topography_codes.json) do not yet list Group 11; its note says to add it when Group 11 is built.
ICCC-2017 places medulloepithelioma at C00-C69 in IVb (behaviour /3 only). Group IV's tree already holds the ciliary body site (op_medulloepithelioma).
The optic nerve is C72.3, a central nervous system site: medulloepithelioma there is IIIc3 and optic nerve glioma is IIIb. The eye site screen refers optic nerve tumours to Group III.
Tissue-free registration records 8000/3, and non-typed malignant cytology records 8000/3; ICCC-2017 places 8000/3 at C69 in XIIb, so these cases leave Group XI when the subgroup is computed.

Malignant mixed tumour (8940/3) and myoepithelial carcinoma (8982/3) of the lacrimal gland are XIIa4 at every site, while carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma (8941/3) is XIf9. The lacrimal screen refers the malignant mixed tumour wording to Group XII. Myoepithelial carcinoma is not in the Milman list and has no option; a report naming it needs the Group XII tree.
Myeloid sarcoma of the orbit is Ib; Group I's tree already holds the orbit (C69.6). Rule E keeps the orbit as its site.
Ocular adnexal and intraocular lymphomas are Group II; Langerhans cell histiocytosis (9751) is IId.
Orbital rhabdomyosarcoma is IXa. Ewing sarcoma of the orbital soft tissue (C69.6) is IXd2, while Ewing sarcoma of the orbital bone (C41.0) is VIIIc2 (Group 8).
Orbital teratoma and yolk sac tumour are Xb at C69; Group X's tree holds the C69 sites.
A tumour of the bone of the orbital wall is recorded at the bone (C41.0), not at the orbit (C69.6).

Inside Group XI: eyelid tumours (sebaceous carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, Merkel cell carcinoma, endocrine mucin-producing sweat gland carcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma of the eyelid) are XIe at C44.1. WHO Eye5 removed sebaceous carcinoma from the conjunctiva chapter. Melanoma (8720-8790) at every eye site is XId and goes to the melanoma tree.

data_gaps.need: A paediatric source for eye carcinomas: conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma (ocular surface squamous neoplasia) in children and adolescents, and lacrimal gland carcinoma (chiefly adenoid cystic carcinoma) in childhood.
data_gaps.why: Neither Milman 2023 nor Pfister 2022 reports any eye carcinoma in a child, so ruling 1 makes every eye carcinoma a picker entry. With a paediatric report, conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma and lacrimal adenoid cystic carcinoma would become options on their site screens.
